随着世界冠军领跑者安东内利将在意大利大奖赛从发车区末位起步，位居积分榜前列、试图追赶他的三位英国车手迎来了重大机会。
安东内利在梅赛德斯的队友拉塞尔和法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿都落后这位意大利车手59分，而卫冕世界冠军兰多·诺里斯凭借最近两场比赛的胜利，将差距缩小到83分。
梅赛德斯决定，尽管蒙扎是安东内利的主场，但这里是这位20岁车手因超出本赛季引擎部件配额而接受处罚的最佳赛道。

由于安东内利在本赛季早些时候因技术问题损失了第二台动力单元，他在某个时刻遭遇发车区罚退已不可避免，而在蒙扎超车预期会比较容易，这让车队和车手都决定在“速度圣殿”接受处罚。
虽然梅赛德斯显然预计安东内利能够在比赛中从后往前追击并拿到积分，但周日的正赛对于他身后的车手们来说仍然是一个巨大的机会，他们可以借此缩小与他之间的积分差距。
在《F1 节目》（The F1 Show）播客中发言时，伯尼·柯林斯认为，在托托·沃尔夫承认车队“没有足够的资金”来匹敌对手的升级之后，梅赛德斯已经把他们的升级“前置”安排了
拉塞尔目前在车手积分榜上排名第二、位于汉密尔顿之上，原因是他赢下了更多分站冠军，他显然不能错过在蒙扎的机会。
虽然夏休期前后在匈牙利和荷兰举行的两场比赛本就不被预期是梅赛德斯的强项赛道，但他们在意大利应该会恢复状态。
然而，赛季上半程意外地被安东内利压过一头，这让拉塞尔对自己的方式产生了疑虑。
观看乔治·拉塞尔赢得荷兰大奖赛冲刺赛，同时兰多·诺里斯把第二位输给了夏尔·勒克莱尔
这位28岁的车手在夏休期后的赞德沃特度过了一个扎实的周末，他赢得了冲刺赛，并在正赛中获得第三名，但在周日正赛速度方面仍然无法与安东内利相匹敌。
考虑到他本赛季晚些时候也将不得不接受一次发车处罚，如果拉塞尔没有取得重大进步，车队可能会倾向于在剩余赛季中优先支持安东内利。
如果拉塞尔未能排在队友之前完赛，这位英国车手的总冠军希望将几乎破灭。
在马克斯·维斯塔潘与红牛续约之后，乔治·拉塞尔和兰多·诺里斯被问及他是否曾构成威胁或引发担忧，并作出了回应
法拉利的引擎升级能否推动汉密尔顿前进？
今年六月，汉密尔顿在巴塞罗那取得他代表法拉利的首场大奖赛胜利时，看似正在发起对总冠军的冲击，但这一势头已逐渐减弱。
自巴塞罗那以来的五场比赛中，车手和车队的失误导致几乎每一站都未能将成绩最大化。
这位七届世界冠军需要一个周末来重振他的争冠势头，还有什么地方比在蒙扎，在车迷（tifosi）面前做到这一点更好的呢？
法拉利车队在主场大奖赛之前面临的最大问题是，他们预计带到蒙扎的引擎升级效果究竟会有多大。
在比赛的最后阶段，法拉利的两位队友险些相撞，而兰多·诺里斯则夺得了荷兰大奖赛的胜利
如果他们在这方面取得重大进步，那么周日红衣车手中的一位完全有机会站上最高领奖台。
对汉密尔顿来说，确保那个人是他自己至关重要，因为他的队友夏尔·勒克莱尔如果获胜，将对他争取创纪录的第八个世界冠军的希望造成重大打击。
汉密尔顿对勒克莱尔的领先优势只有28分，他需要扩大这一分差，才能说服法拉利尽早而非更晚地把支持投向他的夺冠大业。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿对法拉利感到沮丧，因为没有更早地让他和夏尔·勒克莱尔互换位置，他认为这是在“浪费时间”。
状态榜显示，卫冕世界冠军是意大利站夺冠的明显热门，诺里斯在拿下迈凯伦本赛季前两场胜利时展现了超凡的速度。
然而，迈凯伦能否在一条截然不同的赛道上保持状态的回升，仍存在很大疑问。
车队在赛事前瞻中警告称，尽管确认MCL40赛车又迎来了更多升级件，但“本周末他们的整体套件可能并非最快”。
detailEn: Italian GP: Will Lewis Hamilton, George Russell or Lando Norris seize title-race opening due to Kimi Antonelli grid penalties

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is highly unlikely to contend for victory at the Italian Grand Prix, so can his title rivals take advantage? Watch every session of the Italian GP live on Sky Sports, starting with Friday's practice sessions at 11.30am and 3pm
Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza

With world championship leader Kimi Antonelli set to start from the back of the grid at the Italian Grand Prix, the trio of Brits attempting to chase him down at the top of the standings have a major opportunity.

Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both trail the Italian by 59 points, while reigning world champion Lando Norris has reduced his deficit to 83 points with victories at the last two races.
Mercedes have decided that Monza, despite it being Antonelli's home race, is the best circuit for the 20-year-old to incur penalties for exceeding his allowance of engine parts for the season.

With grid penalties inevitable at some point for Antonelli after he lost a second power unit to technical issues earlier in the season, the expected simplicity of overtaking at Monza convinced team and driver to take the Temple of Speed.

While Mercedes clearly anticipate Antonelli will be able to fight back through the field to score points, Sunday's race remains a huge opportunity for those behind him to take a chunk out of his lead.
Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Mercedes have 'front-loaded' their upgrades following Toto Wolff admitting his team 'haven't got the money' to match their rivals' upgrades
Russell, who is above Hamilton in second in the standings because he has won more races, surely cannot afford to miss out at Monza.
Whereas the two races either side of the summer break - in Hungary and the Netherlands - were never expected to be Mercedes' strongest tracks, they should return to form in Italy.
However, being unexpectedly outperformed by Antonelli over the first half of the season has created doubts for Russell around his approach.
Watch George Russell win the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint, as Lando Norris loses second place to Charles Leclerc
The 28-year-old produced a solid weekend in Zandvoort after the break as he won the Sprint and took third in the race, but he was still no match for Antonelli in terms of Sunday pace.

Bearing in mind that he too will have to take a grid penalty at a race later this season, anything other than a major gain for Russell could see the team lean towards prioritising Antonelli for the rest of the campaign.
A scenario where Russell fails to finish ahead of his team-mate would all but end the Brit's title hopes.
Following Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract extension, George Russell and Lando Norris respond to questions about whether he ever posed a threat or caused concern
Will Ferrari engine upgrade propel Hamilton?
The title charge Hamilton appeared to be mounting when he claimed his first Ferrari Grand Prix win in Barcelona back in June has gradually lost momentum.
Errors from both driver and team have contributed to a failure to maximise results in just about all five races since Barcelona.
The seven-time world champion needs a weekend to reinvigorate his challenge, and where better to produce it than in front of the tifosi at Monza?
The big question around Ferrari going into the team's home race is how effective the engine upgrade they are expected to bring to Monza will be.
The Ferrari team-mates nearly came together in the final stages of the race as Lando Norris took the Dutch GP victory
If they take a significant step forward in that department, there is every chance that one of the drivers in red can stand on the top of the podium on Sunday.
It's crucial for Hamilton that he makes sure it's him, because victory for his team-mate Charles Leclerc would represent a major setback for his hopes of claiming a record eighth title.
Hamilton's lead over Leclerc is only 28 points, a figure which he needs to increase to persuade Ferrari to throw their support behind his title aspirations sooner rather than later.
Lewis Hamilton was left frustrated with Ferrari for 'wasting time' by not swapping him and Charles Leclerc earlier
The form guide makes the reigning world champion the clear favourite for victory in Italy, with Norris having showed supreme pace while claiming McLaren's first two wins of the season.
However, there are significant doubts over whether McLaren can maintain their upturn in performance at a vastly different type of circuit.
The team have warned in their event preview that they "may not have the outright quickest package this weekend" despite confirming the arrival of yet more upgrades on the MCL40.

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
